definition: Tokenizers is a fast Rust library, with Python bindings, for training and running BPE, WordPiece and Unigram tokenizers.
details: Developed by Hugging Face (Anthony Moi and team) in 2019.

explainer.lead: How to install Hugging Face Tokenizers, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.

quickstart.python:
from tokenizers import Tokenizer, models, trainers, pre_tokenizers

tok = Tokenizer(models.BPE(unk_token="[UNK]"))
tok.pre_tokenizer = pre_tokenizers.Whitespace()
tok.train(["corpus.txt"], trainers.BpeTrainer(vocab_size=8000, special_tokens=["[UNK]"]))
print(tok.encode("Tokenizers split text into pieces.").tokens)

explainer.inAi: Every Transformers model ships a tokenizer.json built with this library; train your own when working with a new language or domain.

tiers.eli5: Before an AI reads text, it chops it into small pieces like words or word-fragments; this tool does the chopping very quickly.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to train custom tokenizers and to convert raw text into token IDs at high speed inside training and inference code. A pitfall is training a tokenizer on the wrong corpus or with the wrong algorithm, which quietly hurts downstream model quality.
tiers.paperLevel: Stated simply as a Rust library with Python bindings for training and running BPE, WordPiece and Unigram tokenizers; no formal definitions or limits are supplied.

explainer.example: A team building a domain-specific model trains a BPE tokenizer with this library on its own text corpus before starting model training.
